project_folder: CD Prabhakar Reddy Project Id B83CC285

verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 7 and 9 show a ground-mounted PV array sitting on open, sandy farmland with no rooftop/building beneath it at all; the CAD layout on page 7 is explicitly titled 'Lepakshi Farm Land' and notes 'Type of power plant: Ground mounted, On-Grid Power plant'.
verdicts.rationale: Photos and the layout drawing both confirm a ground-mount installation on farmland, consistent with 'Other / Ground-mounted system'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6 and page 9 exterior photos show open farmland around the array with only distant trees/scrub on the horizon; no structures, trees, tanks or walls sit close enough to shade or physically obstruct the panel area.
verdicts.rationale: No obstruction is visible in the immediate vicinity of the array in any exterior photo.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: The Module Mounting Layout drawing on page 7 explicitly states 'Panels Slope: 10 Degrees'. The ground-mount racking in the page 6/9 photos also shows a low, shallow tilt consistent with ~10°.
verdicts.rationale: Direct textual confirmation of 10° on the layout drawing plus a visually shallow tilt in the photos.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.designer_notes: EcoSoch Ground mounted (Ground Mount HDGI with Galvalume)
verdicts.photo_observation: The page 7 layout drawing's notes read 'Type of Structure: EcoSoch Ground mounted'. Photos on pages 6 and 9 show an elevated steel ground-mount rail structure under the panels rather than any roof-mounted rail/rafter system.
verdicts.rationale: Layout drawing text and site photos both confirm a ground-mount structure, matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: The page 7 CAD layout shows a compass rose (N up-left, S down) but the ground-level exterior photos (pages 6, 9) carry no compass or shadow-direction cue that lets the panel-facing direction be independently confirmed.
verdicts.rationale: Orientation can't be reliably read off ground-level photos without a compass reference; the layout drawing alone isn't sufficient to independently verify true facing direction.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.designer_notes: Direct walkable access is available to the farmland.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 7 (Material Delivery Route) and 9 show flat, open farmland with dirt tracks leading directly to the array location — no ladder, staircase, or elevated access is needed since the array sits at ground level.
verdicts.rationale: Ground-level walkable terrain is clearly visible in every exterior photo, matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: The 'Meter Box' photo on page 10 shows a utility pole carrying a 63 kVA transformer, EB meter and termination box, with a couple of overhead conductors on simple pin-type insulators — consistent with an LT service drop rather than a high-tension line, but the exact voltage class and its distance from the actual PV array (which sits further out in the field per pages 6/7/9) can't be confirmed from the photo alone.
verdicts.rationale: The overhead lines shown look like a low-tension service connection rather than an HT line, but voltage class and exact distance to the array aren't independently verifiable from the photo.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: The page 7 'Material Delivery Route' photo shows an open dirt track (traced with a teal route line) running from the shed/yard area into the farmland, wide enough for vehicle access; page 6's yard photo also shows an open, unobstructed dirt approach.
verdicts.rationale: A clear, driveable dirt approach to the unloading/shed area is visible in the photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.photo_observation: The site is open, flat farmland with wide walkable paths and no narrow stairwells, low headroom, or tight corners visible in any of the exterior photos.
verdicts.rationale: No lifting obstacles are visible; the ground-mount, at-grade layout removes typical rooftop lifting constraints.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: All accessories can be located inside the nearby shed allocated as the inverter room (where a 70 kW battery-based solar inverter and related accessories exists).
verdicts.photo_observation: The page 10 'Equipment Location' photo shows a shed interior with labeled DC-DB, INVERTER, and AC-DB enclosures mounted on the wall, plus an existing white inverter-like unit visible at the right of the frame consistent with the mentioned existing 70kW inverter.
verdicts.rationale: The photo directly shows the DCDB/Inverter/ACDB equipment installed inside the shed described.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 8 and 10 show the equipment fully enclosed inside a roofed metal shed, sheltered from weather already.
verdicts.rationale: Equipment is indoors under an existing roof, so no additional canopy is needed, matching the 'No' answer.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_answer: Yes, discussed with the site-in-charge and finalised the location for earthing.
verdicts.photo_observation: The page 9 'Cable Routing' photo has 'AC Earth Pit' and 'DC Earth Pit' location markers annotated next to the shed, indicating specific earthing locations were identified and marked on site.
verdicts.rationale: Finalized earth pit locations are annotated on the site photo, consistent with a discussed/agreed location, though the discussion itself (a conversation) isn't something a photo can directly confirm.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.designer_answer: The router is available inside the inverter room shed.
verdicts.photo_observation: The shed interior photos (pages 8, 10) show the DCDB/Inverter/ACDB equipment and tools, but no distinct router/networking device is visible or labeled in either photo.
verdicts.rationale: No router is visibly identifiable in the shed photos, so the specific location claim can't be confirmed or contradicted.

verdicts.photo_observation: Signal strength is not a visually verifiable attribute and no phone/signal-indicator screenshot is included in the photo documentation.

verdicts.question: Is a Lightning Arrestor (LA) already available at the site?

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?

The page 9 cable-routing photo also marks 'Solar Meter' as a separate annotated location next to 'Main Meter', not inside the same panel, consistent with needing a new fabricated provision.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: Because of the rough terrain beneath, piling of the footposts can be challenging. However, in order to meet the need, the client is willing to provide support and machinery.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6's photos show uneven, clumpy soil with plant/root debris and loose sandy patches around the array area, consistent with 'rough terrain' that could complicate footpost piling.
verdicts.rationale: Visible uneven, debris-strewn ground around the array supports the claim of challenging terrain for foundation work.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?

verdicts.rationale: No elevated/roof access is required for this ground-mount system, matching the 'No' answer.

verdicts.designer_answer: All of the accessories must be installed on a metal grill that will be built within the shed designated for solar power.

verdicts.rationale: The mounting hardware visible behind the enclosures looks like a metal frame/rail rather than a direct wall mount, consistent with a metal-grill mounting plan.

verdicts.question: Is there any trench work to be done to carry the AC cable to the meter location?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: A trench must be excavated in order to carry the DC wires from the intended location to the inverter-room shed.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6's second photo shows disturbed/mounded soil and a gravel-lined patch near the shed consistent with prepared or planned trench/cable-route excavation; the page 7 layout drawing also marks a 'Solar DC cable trench' line running from the array to the DCDB/Inverter/ACDB location.
verdicts.rationale: Visible disturbed soil near the routing path plus an explicit 'DC cable trench' line on the layout drawing both support planned trenching work.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Indoors (page 10, 'Equipment Location'), the DC-DB → INVERTER → AC-DB run is color-coded and continuous, with the AC line then following a visible conduit toward the meter panel and an existing unit at the shed's edge — no orphan ends indoors. Outdoors (page 9, 'Cable Routing'), an annotated overlay traces green/red/purple lines from the shed through 'AC Earth Pit' and 'DC Earth Pit' markers out to the 'Proposed location for 58 Nos. of PV modules', again with no visible orphan ends in the diagram. However, this outdoor routing is a planned/annotated overlay on a pre-installation site photo, not an as-built photograph of a physically continuous, buried cable run, so end-to-end physical continuity in the field can't be independently confirmed from these images alone.
verdicts.rationale: The indoor equipment run is genuinely continuous in the photo, and the outdoor overlay diagram shows a coherent planned path with no orphan ends, but the outdoor cable run itself is planned/annotated rather than a photograph of installed, physically continuous cable, so full as-built continuity cannot be verified from a pre-installation TSVR.
